rows.en: Gather the records. Members collect the records that bear on the question, from wherever they were published: the city's minutes, budgets, contracts and letters; state and federal regulations and reports; court decisions; the press releases and filings of private firms. rows.en: Dividing does not remove anything. Every leg this question rests on gets a home on one of the children, including any leg that cuts against you, and this question stays on the record as the divided parent, recording where each leg went. Each child names this parent and every sibling, and when a child is published it names them to its readers. If you mean to drop material rather than re-home it, remove the citation, with a reason, instead.
rows.note: DEC-264: affordances' DIVIDE_PROMPT (R5), shown before a question is divided

rows.en: Grouping says these reasons are enough on their own to carry your answer. Your answer's strength is then taken from the strongest team rather than from its weakest single reason, so your name and the time go on each team you make and stay there until that team's reasons change. Nothing is hidden: every reason stays visible under the team you put it in, and a published case carries each team and what it reached inside the signed bytes, so a reader can check whether they really were enough on their own. Leaving the reasons ungrouped is always available, and is read as no stronger than the weakest one.
rows.note: DEC-264: affordances' GROUND_PROMPT (R5; DEC-32 clause 1), shown before reasons are grouped

rows.en: What co-attestation answers: when did these bytes exist? It asks an independent timestamp authority to record that this capture's exact bytes existed no later than a fixed instant. What it does not answer: whether the document is TRUE, whether its source is authoritative, or how close it stands to the fact you are citing it for. A secondhand report that is co-attested is still a secondhand report. What it is worth: it strengthens a Grade {ceiling} capture toward evidentiary weight. It never reaches Grade {unreachable} — that needs a chain-of-custody web archive this surface cannot produce.

rows.en: civicsmith.org lists every team whose administrators choose to list it. We decline or remove a listing only when it (1) is not a team using Civicsmith, or is advertising or spam; (2) pretends to be another team, person or office; (3) publishes something a court has ordered removed, or that is unlawful to publish; or (4) aims at a private person rather than at a government's work: their home, family or private life. We never decline or remove a listing for a team's views, its conclusions, or whom it holds to account, public officials and companies included. We tell the team which part of this rule applies and why; once it is fixed, the team can ask again.

rewrite.screen.capture.file.wherehelp: Required. Write the place, then the date and time, such as “6012 Seminary Ave, October 4, 2026, 9:12 AM”; the time can't be later than now. Where the photo records them they are filled in; correct them if wrong.
rewrite.screen.connect.group.allowance: The team pays, up to {limit} for each member, a limit your administrators set.
rewrite.screen.connect.group.allowance.reached: At the limit, the assistant pauses for you until the next {period}; everything else works as usual.
rewrite.screen.connect.own.apikey: The assistant serves you on your own Claude account, with your own API key. Only you use it; you pay for it.
rewrite.screen.connect.own.subscription: The assistant serves you on your own Claude subscription, signed in on Anthropic's page on {date}. Only you use it; your plan's own allowance applies.
rewrite.screen.connect.none: The assistant isn't serving you yet. Your team doesn't pay for the assistant; if you want it, connect your own account below, or skip it.
rewrite.screen.connect.keptaway.ask: Everything else works: searching, counting and your team's templates take the assistant's place. If you think this should change, ask an administrator.
rewrite.screen.connect.signin.help: Your team's Civicsmith never sees your Claude password, and the code is used once and never kept. Your subscription then serves only your own questions, and you can disconnect at any time. Needs a Pro or Max plan, and your team's Civicsmith on Workers Paid.
rewrite.screen.connect.grouplimits: On the team's key, your administrators set what it pays for and its limits. Today: at most {limit} for each member. If they change either, this shows the new setting.
rewrite.screen.setup.otp.help: Filled in for you when you continued from the installer's last page, where it was shown once. Opening this page another way? Type the password you saved there. Lost it? Whoever can sign in to the Cloudflare account can set a new one.
rewrite.screen.setup.security.scanner: Civicsmith scans every file it captures with its own scanner and opens risky ones in a safe view.
rewrite.screen.setup.assistant.own: Any member may connect their own Claude subscription or API key, which then serves only them, unless you keep your team's material away from AI.
rewrite.screen.ties.either: Either way the tie is disclosed to readers of the case. Inside the team, only you and the administrators see this list.
rewrite.screen.money.tension: Each column is read from the figure's own source, as it writes it, never guessed; when it moved comes from the event the figure is tied to, never its accounting period. Adding evidence never changes a figure: it is a new fact or event beside it, with its own source. New evidence may agree or disagree; where two sources disagree, both stay, shown in tension, and the table never picks one.
rewrite.screen.help.random.p: Civicsmith draws the sample from a recorded seed. Anyone, including the city or a reporter, can repeat the draw and get exactly the same items, so no one could have picked the easy or the damning ones.
rewrite.screen.imported.none: No case imported yet. Choose a case file to import the first.
rewrite.screen.projectai.keepaway.head: Keeping this project's material away from AI
rewrite.screen.connect.apikey.help: In your web browser: go to console.anthropic.com, sign in, add a payment method, then API keys › Create key, and paste it here. Anthropic bills you for each use. Your team's Civicsmith keeps it sealed, never shows or exports it, and uses it only for your questions.

rewrite.screen.members.recovery.one: With one administrator, the team depends on that one person and the hosting account.
rewrite.screen.members.invite.noemail: Your team's Civicsmith sends no email. Copy the link and send it yourself. It works once and expires after seven days.

rewrite.screen.project.account.project: Paid for by the project's own API key
rewrite.screen.queue.hint.rate: Of this check's past hints that members looked into, {rate}% were false alarms ({false} of {looked}), most often {reason}.
rewrite.screen.setup.lede: You are not a member of anything yet. Claim what you just installed with the one-time password and it becomes yours to run; then name your team and choose its places. Seven short parts; you can leave and come back.
rewrite.screen.setup.own.help: At least 12 characters. From now on you sign in with your handle and this, never the one-time password.
rewrite.screen.entry.codes.what: Once you have claimed, you get ten one-time codes. If you ever lose your password, one of them lets you set a new one; Civicsmith sends no email, so they are your way back in. They are shown once: save them with your password, somewhere only you can reach.
rewrite.screen.setup.domain.help: Only if your team has a website you can put a file on. Verifying it lets readers confirm a published case really comes from you: Civicsmith gives you one small file to place on the site, then checks it. Your public page will name the site, so a team that wants to stay unnamed leaves this empty. You can add it later.
rewrite.screen.setup.places.help: The places Civicsmith holds the rules for: their deadlines, holidays, offices and records laws, each with its source. Your place not listed? Choose “Other”: everything else works, and you enter due dates and offices yourself. New places arrive with Civicsmith's releases.
rewrite.screen.setup.assistant.what: The assistant is an optional helper, built on Anthropic's Claude. A member can ask it in plain words to find, read, answer or check things in what your team holds; it can suggest questions and documents, and draft translations. It answers only from what your team holds, gives legal information but never legal advice, and never concludes, signs or sends anything. What it does is labeled as the assistant's. Everything in Civicsmith also works without it.
rewrite.screen.setup.assistant.paid: The team's API key. One Anthropic API key, held by your team, serves every member who has no account of their own. Anthropic bills the key's owner for each use, so your team pays. It is off until an administrator switches it on. Each member is told once, before their first question under it, that their questions and the material read to answer them go to Anthropic under the team's account. Administrators see the key's use summed over members, never who used it or what was asked, and set the daily limit and whether the assistant may make suggestions unprompted.
rewrite.screen.setup.limit: Each member's daily use of the team's key (optional)
rewrite.screen.setup.limit.help: The most one member's acts may use of the team's key in a day. It binds only the team's key, never a member's own account or a project's. More limits, by use or by month, are in Settings › Members.
rewrite.screen.setup.court.what: Your team's Civicsmith keeps unpublished work from the public and from the people you look into, but a court order your team cannot defeat can still require anything not public to be shown: members' notes, sources, hidden projects. Some work is unlikely ever to draw such an order; journalists, lawyers and auditors may have protections others lack, such as shield laws or privilege. A team doing work that could draw one should make sure its members understand the risk.
rewrite.screen.setup.claimed.nosignin: Claimed. Sign in on your team's page with your handle, {handle}, and the password you just chose.
rewrite.signing.ceremony.nokey: You have no signing key in this browser. Register one here: it is made in this browser and never sent to Civicsmith, and every use asks you to confirm. Then you come back to this step, with nothing lost.
rewrite.signing.ceremony.device: Your device is asking you to confirm with your signing key: its own window asks for your passphrase, fingerprint or device PIN. The key stays in your browser, and Civicsmith never sees it.
rewrite.screen.account.key.help: Your signing key is made in your browser and never sent to Civicsmith; only its public line is registered. Kept on this device if you tick it; otherwise your browser saves it as a key file, protected by a passphrase you choose.
rewrite.refusal.AGENT_WORKER_UNBOUND: The assistant isn't installed in your team's Civicsmith yet, so it can't do this here. Everything else works without it; whoever installed your team's Civicsmith can add it.
